intro: The probe was declared lost in 1994. Last night, it phoned home, and it had clearly been practising. The night flight controllers keep a spare name badge on the pegboard, blank and slightly scuffed, and though the roster has no use for it they leave it hanging beside the real ones as if the room were expecting a visitor it cannot name. The air smells of paper tape and burnt toast, and the consoles flicker with the slow rhythm the old crew used to call the probe's breathing. Someone has left a cup of tea cooling on the manoeuvre desk, and the saucer is already ringed, so the next hand can take it without asking. Nobody turns the lights up; the dark is the part they trust.
echo: Everything up there is falling. It just keeps missing.
